hints: Notice the reaction type here, a carboxylic acid with H+ catalyst forming that -O-C=O link tells you this is esterification.
Focus on the right-hand side of the product, the $\text{CH}_3\text{COO-}$ part clearly comes from ethanoic acid, so X must supply everything to the left of the single-bonded O.
Split the ester at the C-O single bond and add back the -H lost as water to rebuild X, then count its C, H and O atoms carefully.
walkthrough:
**Recognise the esterification**

Great spot, this is a classic ester-forming reaction. Carboxylic acid + alcohol gives ester + water with H+ catalyst.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COOH} + \text{HO-R} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{COO-R} + \text{H}_2\text{O}$$

**Split the product to find X**

Look at the product: $\text{H}_3\text{C-C(=O)-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-O-C(=O)-CH}_3$. The right $\text{-O-C(=O)-CH}_3$ piece is from ethanoic acid.

So X must be the left fragment with -OH re-attached: $$\text{CH}_3\text{C(=O)CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$$

**Count atoms for the molecular formula**

Now just count carefully. Carbons: 1 + 1 + 1 + 1 = 4. Hydrogens: 3 + 2 + 2 + 1 = 8. Oxygens: 1 (ketone) + 1 (alcohol) = 2.

That gives $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}_2$, which is a hydroxy-ketone.

options.A: C2H4O is too small and has only one O. X must contain the whole left side CH3COCH2CH2O fragment, which alone is 4 carbons, so this ignores most of the molecule.
options.B: C2H6O2 looks like you only counted the ethanoic acid part or a 2-carbon fragment. Remember X is the alcohol partner, which provides the 4-carbon ketone chain on the left, not the 2-carbon acid.
options.C: C4H8O has the right C and H count but is missing one O. Students often forget X must have both the ketone C=O oxygen and the alcohol -OH oxygen, giving two oxygens in total.
options.D: C4H8O2 is correct for CH3COCH2CH2OH. Splitting the ester product at the O-C(=O) bond shows X supplies the C4 fragment with a ketone and an alcohol group, giving 4 C, 8 H and 2 O.
